pages.observations: Printed4 Introduction. Tool T relative to station S is input; explicitly find wrist W relative to base B then joint angles. Figure labels camera, tool, pin, wrist, station, goal and base; a blank outlined rectangle is not evidence.

Printed5 Solvability. Product of six transforms; rotation R and position P block. Six independent pose quantities versus six joints, with nonlinear/transcendental equations. Some text behind the transform figure is visually occluded, but the six-equations bullet is clear.
Printed6 lists existence, multiple solutions and method as distinct IK challenges.

Printed7 distinguishes all-orientation dextrous workspace from at-least-one-orientation reachable workspace. Planar2R equal links give radius2L disc with origin dextrous point; unequal links give annulus and no dextrous workspace. Inner radius printed L1−L2 needs length-order qualification or absolute value; source diagram has only two links.

Printed8 Multiple solutions. Compute branches then choose; small joint motion preferred unless obstacle needs alternative. Diagram contrasts dashed large-motion elbow configuration around obstacle. PUMA560 can have eight, not every target must. Broad link-parameter monotonicity wording needs table qualification.
Printed9 6R table rows a1=a3=a5=0→≤4; a3=a5=0→≤8; a3=0→≤16; all ai≠0→≤16. Final rows plainly same upper bound, contrary to interpreting footer as strict increase.

Printed10 has literal f(αx)=αx typo, solvable defined as unique despite later branch discussion, numerical iterative, algebraic identities/substitution, geometric law of cosines, colloquial sub-space examples circle/plane and sphere/XYZ. These are recorded as source issues, not silently accepted mathematical definitions.

Printed11 calls six-DOF R/P serial systems solvable numerically, favors intersecting axes and many αi=0 or90°, defines algorithmic solvability and asks for all joint solutions. Broad numerical claim cannot imply reachability/convergence for every target.

Printed12 separates iterative numerical from algebraic/geometric closed form; analytical preferred for computation time. Sufficient6R condition is three neighboring axes intersecting at one point, not a necessary-condition statement or global reachability guarantee.

Printed13 Kinematics: spherical wrist has three common-point joint axes. Figure labels joint4 wrist rotation, joint5 wrist bend, joint6 flange rotation, with distinct axes drawn. Text mentions Pieper closed form and quarter-table trig symmetry.

Printed14 planar3R FK matrix has orientation cos/sin(θ1+θ2+θ3), but translation only l1cosθ1+l2cos(θ1+θ2), l1sinθ1+l2sin(θ1+θ2). DH rows have a0=0,a1=L1,a2=L2 and all α,d zero; no L3 tool displacement. Figure shows frame3 at tip and rotatable orientation.
Printed15 derives squared radius L1²+L2²+2L1L2cosθ2, then c2 ratio, s2=±sqrt(1−c2²), θ2=atan2(s2,c2). Out-of-range described as far away, but inner hole is also impossible; boundary sin terms vanish.

Printed16 gives k1=L1+L2c2,k2=L2s2, r=sqrt(k1²+k2²), γ=atan2(k2,k1). Triangle labels k1 horizontal,k2 vertical,r diagonal,γ at left. First x expression is correct; middle normalized x line wrongly ends −sinγcosθ1. Final cosine-sum and shoulder atan2 difference are correct for r>0.

Printed17 explicitly notes undefined shoulder formula at x=y=0 and arbitrary θ1; this requires the point to be reachable (equal links). Sum θ1+θ2+θ3=atan2(sφ,cφ)=φ needs modulo2π interpretation. Final paragraph describes algebraic manipulation, not numerical iteration.

Printed19 geometric triangle contains both elbow branches with θ2 and θ2prime=−θ2. Negative branch interval stated0 to−180; text overclaims only those values while the next bullet restores reflection. Outer-distance bound appears but lower annulus bound is omitted. β=atan2(y,x), cosψ=(x²+y²+L1²−L2²)/(2L1sqrt(x²+y²)).

Printed20 ψ in[0,180], shoulder β±ψ with plus for negative elbow, minus for positive. Correct angle-sum equation precedes erroneous final θ3=φ−θ1+θ2. Diagram repeats both elbow configurations; repair must retain negative sign on both subtracted joint angles.

Printed21 differential drive. ul,ur explicitly wheel angular rates; vl=rul,vr=rur. qdot ordered[φdot,xdot,ydot]. J is3×2 with rows[−r/(2d),r/(2d)],[(r/2)cosφ,(r/2)cosφ],[(r/2)sinφ,(r/2)sinφ]. Sketch marks half-trackd and headingφ.

Printed22 prose maps desired(v,ω) to individual wheel rates. Equation pdot=[ul,ur]=J^-1 qdot uses inverse notation despite rectangularJ. Forward diagram reverses qdot andpdot labels relative to p289 equation; both diagram and inverse notation must be explicitly qualified.

Printed23 states full rank=min(m,n). Tall m>n formula (J^TJ)^−1J^T; wide m<n formula J^T(JJ^T)^−1. Differential3×2 uses tall case. Printed shortcuts require rank; general pseudoinverse still exists at rank deficiency.
Printed24 derives average v=r(ur+ul)/2 and yawω=r(ur−ul)/(2d), then ur=(v+dω)/r andul=(v−dω)/r. Sign corresponds to positive yaw when right wheel is faster.

Printed25 summary distinguishes desired-pose→joint-configuration IK, analytic special geometries, more general Jacobian-based numerical methods needing singularity handling, and differential desired(v,ω)→wheel rates.
